svg.title: iOS · Fullscreen media player (video) · portrait
svg.desc: Mirrors App/FullscreenMediaSheet.swift (FullscreenMediaSheet chrome + FullscreenVideoPage) — the one in-app player, presented as a fullScreenCover on iOS/iPadOS and as a sheet on macOS (which has no fullScreenCover). Every playback tap on project detail lands here: the grading card's play button, a source clip row, a version row. Black to the edges, status bar hidden. Chrome: a 36pt circular × top-left, the "n of m" position between, and a 36pt circular share button top-right (share is omitted, and its space held, for the two items that exist only in memory — a stitched multi-segment take and an interval motion preview — since there is no single file to hand over). Below the video, a scrubber appears once AVPlayerItem.duration resolves above zero: an accent slider with elapsed left and total right, over a 35% black plate. Playback autoplays, loops (actionAtItemEnd = .none plus a seek on AVPlayerItemDidPlayToEndTime), and only the visible page plays — the pager pauses the others. VideoPlayer's own transport also appears on tap and auto-hides; this scrubber is the sheet's, always on. Swipe left/right pages through the siblings the caller passed (the project's other source clips, its other versions) via TabView .page(indexDisplayMode: .never), so the dots are NOT drawn — position is text. Swipe down past 120pt dismisses (a DragGesture that only claims clearly vertical drags, so paging keeps horizontal ones). A non-identity project grade is applied live through VideoGrader.composition — nothing is baked, nothing is written to disk. Two variants are not drawn: `.intervalMotion` replaces the scrubber with a transport row (play/pause circle · "12 / 184" · "12 fps preview"), and `.photo` with a capture id hands the whole surface to PhotoViewerView, whose own Done bar replaces this chrome.
